title: Trump Confirms ‘Minor’ Iran Strikes as Talks Continue and Republicans Split
dek: Trump says U.S. forces knocked out an Iranian air-defense system in a “minor” strike, while talks with Tehran continue and a Republican push to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains in play.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Electronic market-price display with rows of financial information

keyPoints: Trump told reporters Friday that U.S. forces carried out “minor” strikes and knocked out an Iranian anti-aircraft system in about 15 minutes, the Guardian and CNBC reported.
Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz; CNBC said Trump did not explicitly confirm those were the strikes he described.
Trump said the United States is talking with Iran; U.S. Central Command publicized a Rewards for Justice offer of up to $20 million for information on Iran’s nuclear program.
Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, plans to present articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth next week, the Los Angeles Times reported.
body:
President Donald Trump is weighing whether to resume a wider war with Iran or pursue an agreement, and he has now publicly described another round of limited U.S. strikes. The political ground under that choice shifted after Republicans lost ground in the midterm elections.

## Trump describes “minor” strikes

Speaking to reporters on Friday, Trump said the United States carried out “minor” strikes and that “they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five,” [the Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/07/us-carries-out-another-round-of-minor-strikes-on-iran-trump-says) reported. Iranian state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, in the Strait of Hormuz, the Guardian said.

[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/07/trump-us-minor-strikes-iran-qeshm-island.html) reported that Trump did not explicitly confirm that the strikes he described were the reported hits on Qeshm. After landing in West Palm Beach, Florida, he told reporters, “I don’t want to talk about it,” then described knocking out the anti-aircraft device. CNBC, citing Iranian news agency Tasnim via Reuters, said there was no official information on damage.

The Guardian said Friday’s strikes were the first since Republicans lost ground in Tuesday’s midterm elections. The Los Angeles Times had separately reported that the U.S. carried out limited strikes on Iran on Friday and that two U.S. officials said a renewal of all-out attacks remained a distinct possibility.

## Talks continue, reward offered

Trump said Friday, “We are talking to Iran. We have been,” according to the Guardian. CNBC reported that he also said Iran wants “to make a deal very badly,” citing inflation and damage to Iran’s navy and airports; those characterizations are Trump’s, not independently verified figures.

The Guardian reported that U.S. Central Command posted that Rewards for Justice was offering “a reward of up to $20m and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program.” [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/07/middleeast/trump-reward-intelligence-iran-nuclear-program-intl) reported that the State Department program is seeking tips on facilities, equipment and associated personnel, and that relocation may be offered to informants.

Qatar has been mediating. The Guardian, citing the Qatari government, said Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth spoke Friday with his Qatari counterpart, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, and that Trump separately spoke with Qatar’s emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, about de-escalation.

## Hegseth under pressure

The LA Times reported that Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, plans to present articles of impeachment against Hegseth next week over his role overseeing the war effort, and that the measure is expected to gain enough Republican support to pass. The paper also reported that Trump has been surveying advisers about Hegseth’s performance, while publicly maintaining support for him. Hegseth has faced scrutiny over allegations that he misled Trump about the war’s risks to commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

## Vance’s position

The LA Times described a “statement of brazen defiance” from Vice President JD Vance opposing the war. In a post on X, Vance said Republican voters cast ballots for Democrats partly because of frustration over the conflict, the cost of living and U.S. support of Israel, The National reported.

## What we do not know

Meridian has not verified the precise target list, damage on Qeshm Island, whether a larger operation is imminent, or when a House impeachment vote would occur.
